description: Comprehensive security requirements for centralized cryptocurrency exchanges, custodial wallets, and financial Web3 applications.

levels.Level 1: Standard security baseline: Multi-signature or MPC custody, basic hot/cold separation, dual control on key generation.
levels.Level 2: Enhanced enterprise security: Hardware security modules (HSMs, FIPS 140-2/3 Level 3), automated velocity limits, tamper-proof WORM audit logs, geographic seed distribution.
levels.Level 3: Institutional banking-grade: Zero-trust MPC quorum, hardware-isolated air-gapped signing ceremony, real-time Merkle tree Proof of Reserves, biometric/FIDO2 hardware dual authorization.

aspects.name: Key / Seed Generation

criteria.level_1: Keys/seeds generated using a cryptographically secure pseudo-random number generator (CSPRNG).
criteria.level_2: Keys generated inside an air-gapped environment or certified HSM with hardware entropy source.
criteria.level_3: Multi-party ceremony with independent keyholders, video audit log, and Shamir Secret Sharing.

risks: Deterministic or weak PRNG leading to private key derivation and catastrophic fund drainage.

aspects.name: Key / Seed Storage

criteria.level_1: Private keys encrypted at rest using AES-256-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305.
criteria.level_2: Keys stored in FIPS 140-2/3 Level 3 Hardware Security Modules (HSMs) or AWS CloudHSM / HashiCorp Vault.
criteria.level_3: Pure Multi-Party Computation (MPC) threshold scheme with key shares never reconstructed in a single memory space.

risks: Direct plaintext key storage or weak encryption enabling server compromise to result in private key exfiltration.

aspects.name: Key / Seed Usage & Multi-Signature Quorum

criteria.level_1: Single signatures prohibited for master/custody wallets. Minimum 2-of-3 multi-sig or 2-of-2 MPC.
criteria.level_2: Minimum 3-of-5 threshold multi-sig with distinct physical keyholders across separate networks.
criteria.level_3: Dynamic threshold quorums with biometric hardware confirmation (FIDO2/WebAuthn) and time-bounded signing sessions.

risks: Single Point of Failure (SPoF) where compromise of one server/admin authorizes arbitrary fund transfers.

aspects.name: Key Compromise & Revocation Policy

criteria.level_1: Documented emergency procedure for key revocation and fund migration to recovery address.
criteria.level_2: Automated emergency circuit-breaker (freeze contracts / pause transfers) triggered by anomaly detection.
criteria.level_3: Hardware-enforced instant quorum rotation without service interruption or fund exposure.

risks: Inability to halt ongoing theft when an operator key or API gateway is compromised.

aspects.name: Hot / Cold Wallet Asset Allocation

criteria.level_1: Strict separation between Hot Wallet (online) and Cold Storage (offline/air-gapped).
criteria.level_2: Hot Wallet balance capped at maximum 5% of total exchange reserves with automated sweeps to cold storage.
criteria.level_3: Cold storage 100% air-gapped with deep vault geographic separation and multi-institution custody (e.g. BitGo/Fireblocks).

risks: Stray funds accumulating in online hot wallets, making the exchange an attractive honeypot for attackers.

aspects.name: Transaction Verification & Velocity Limits

criteria.level_1: Mandatory 2FA (TOTP/SMS) on all customer and administrative withdrawal requests.
criteria.level_2: Tiered velocity limits (hourly/daily volume caps) + mandatory 24-hour time-lock on new withdrawal address whitelists.
criteria.level_3: Automated behavioral risk scoring + manual dual-operator sign-off on transactions exceeding threshold.

risks: Automated draining of customer balances via unauthorized bulk withdrawal requests.

aspects.name: Proof of Reserves & Solvency Verification

criteria.level_1: Internal automated daily reconciliation between off-chain user ledger and on-chain blockchain balances.
criteria.level_2: Cryptographic Merkle Tree Proof of Reserves published publicly on a periodic schedule (e.g. monthly).
criteria.level_3: Real-time zk-SNARK based Proof of Solvency proving reserves >= liabilities without revealing user balances.

risks: Fractional reserve insolvency, unbacked withdrawals, and off-chain ledger discrepancy.

aspects.name: Tamper-Proof Audit Logging

criteria.level_1: Centralized logging of all administrative actions, logins, and financial transactions with NTP time-sync.
criteria.level_2: Immutable, append-only WORM storage (Write Once Read Many) or S3 Object Lock for audit trails.
criteria.level_3: Cryptographically chained audit logs (hash-chained or signed by KMS) with real-time SIEM alerting.

risks: Attackers deleting or altering logs after intrusion to conceal fund theft.

aspects.name: Dual Control & Segregation of Duties

criteria.level_1: No single engineer has access to both hot wallet signing keys and database ledger modification rights.
criteria.level_2: Mandatory dual-authorization (four-eyes principle) for all operational adjustments to fees, limits, or trading pairs.
criteria.level_3: Strict separation of infrastructure access, cryptographic keys, and application code deployment quorums.

risks: Rogue insider or compromised employee account unilaterally manipulating customer balances.

aspects.name: Disaster Recovery & Redundancy

criteria.level_1: Encrypted off-site backups of database ledger and configuration state tested quarterly.
criteria.level_2: Multi-region active-passive failover with automated state synchronization and RPO < 1 minute.
criteria.level_3: Geographically distributed Shamir Secret Sharing (SSS) key shares across 3+ independent jurisdictions.

risks: Permanent loss of access to cold storage or ledger corruption in case of catastrophic data center outage.
